faq.a: Abdulaziz is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ الْعَزِيز, whose core sense is abdulaziz; servant of the mighty.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulaziz?
faq.a: Abdulaziz is associated with Arabic. Abdulaziz is Arabic عَبْدُ الْعَزِيز (ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz), meaning 'servant of the Mighty'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْعَزِيز is Arabic.
Abdulaziz can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdulaziz should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdulaziz mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdulaziz is rendered عبدالعزیز and carries the sense عبدالعزیز، عزیز کا بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdulaziz mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdulaziz is rendered عبدالعزیز and carries the sense عبدالعزیز، بنده عزیز.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-du-la-ziz. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdulaziz, abdulaziz. Script forms are عبدالعزيز, عبدالعزیز, عَبْدُ الْعَزِيز, अब्दुलअज़ीज़.
